role.altitude: The pharmacy aide keeps helping patients at the counter and on the phone, checking labels and working insurer rejections; typing prescriptions from paper, posting bill lines, working out copayments and typing amounts into the card terminal shrink.
skills_to_grow: Reading insurer rejection codes and fixing their causes at the source
role.ambitious_version: An aide who spends the time saved on claims and labels explaining medicines to patients at the counter.

tasks.short: Check each patient's insurance, post bill amounts for dispensed items, calculate copayments, resolve flagged lines, have the claim batch approved, send it to insurers and process medical insurance claims rejections.

steps.what: Pharmacy aide checks the patient's insurance coverage before dispensing
Pharmacy aide posts bill amounts for each dispensed item
Pharmacy aide calculates copayments: statutory contribution, deductible and items not covered
Pharmacy aide resolves lines flagged before the claim batch
Pharmacy manager reviews totals and approves the final claim batch
Pharmacy aide sends the approved claim batch to the insurers
Pharmacy aide processes rejected claims returned by insurers

approvals.approved_version: the claim batch as approved by the pharmacy manager in s5; lines changed afterwards go into the next batch

tasks.design: The coverage check runs automatically against the insurers' coverage service when a prescription is entered, and the aide handles only failures. Each dispensing record creates its bill line with the price from the national drug tariff database. Fixed rules compute the statutory contribution, deductible and non-covered amounts from the tariff tables and the patient's policy, and flag lines with missing or odd data. The aide resolves flags, the pharmacy manager approves the batch, and the aide sends it. Rejections come back with standard codes that the system groups by cause. No model is used.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bill lines and copayments were keyed or corrected by hand for many items.
tasks.enabler_now: Pharmacy systems with tariff tables, coverage checks and standard claim messages.
tasks.still_hard: Rejections that need a new prescription or a call to the insurer.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining an unexpected copayment to a patient.
tasks.altitude: Much less keying; rejections and patient questions stay.

reach.learn: Whether rejection rates fall when causes are grouped.

evidence.claim: Tariff tables, standard claim messages and arithmetic cover billing, claims and copayments without a model.
Health data are a special category; care use rests on Art. 9(2)(h) with professional secrecy.

assumptions: Boundary: from coverage check to resolved rejections; collecting copayments at the till is a separate task.
Input contract for s2: dispensing records made by the pharmacy assistant in the pharmacy system, with prices from the national drug tariff database updated monthly by its publisher.
Input contract for s3: the patient's policy from the coverage check and the tariff tables; about 85% of lines are computed without a flag; s3 is priced at that share.
Approving and sending keep their full time; the manager's time is outside the aide's savings.

already_counted.description: Pharmacy aide checks lines the rules flag before the batch.

incremental.description: Pharmacy aide checks the monthly tariff update report for changed copayments.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many patients with unusual policies and frequent rejections; high: mostly standard policies with lines computed without flags.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Answer telephone inquiries about prescriptions, stock and opening hours, take repeat prescription requests, refer callers to the pharmacist when necessary and note the outcome.

steps.what: Patient records a repeat prescription request on the phone line or online form
Pharmacy aide answers telephone inquiries about prescriptions, stock and opening hours
Pharmacy aide takes repeat prescription requests and enters them in the pharmacy system
Pharmacy aide refers callers with medical questions to the pharmacist when necessary
Pharmacy aide notes the call outcome in the patient record

tasks.design: A fixed phone menu sends repeat prescription requests to a recorded line, and an online form lets patients choose from their own repeat medicines, which fills the request in the pharmacy system. Other calls go to an aide as today. Medical questions are referred to the pharmacist. Call notes use short pick lists in the patient record. No voice bot is used.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeat requests were taken by phone and written down during the call.
tasks.enabler_now: Repeat prescription lines and online forms linked to pharmacy systems.
tasks.still_hard: Worried callers whose question is really medical.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing that a caller is confused about their medicine.
tasks.altitude: Fewer routine calls; the conversations that matter stay.

reach.learn: Whether referred calls are better prepared.

evidence.claim: Repeat prescription lines and online forms can feed requests into pharmacy systems.
A phone bot must tell callers they speak to AI; the design uses a fixed menu instead.

assumptions: Boundary: answering and routing phone inquiries; the pharmacist's answers are outside.

Input contract for s3: requests from the online form (filled by patients from their repeat list) and the recorded line; about half of repeat requests arrive by form; recorded messages are still typed; s3 is priced at that share.
Patients' effort on the line or form is about what a call took and sits in s1.
Answering and referring keep their full or nearly full time.
unknowns: Share of patients who use the online form.
research_questions: Do call queues at peak hours shorten?

incremental.description: Pharmacy aide clears the recorded line queue twice a day.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older patients who keep calling; high: many patients using the online form.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Enter prescription details, select the dosage instructions, prepare prescription labels by operating a computer and printer, and check each label against the prescription.

steps.what: Pharmacy aide enters prescription details by typing from paper or fax
Pharmacy aide selects the dosage instruction text for the label
Pharmacy aide prints and attaches the prescription labels
Pharmacy aide checks each label against the prescription

tasks.design: Electronic prescriptions sent by prescribers' systems fill the prescription in the pharmacy system, so the aide checks the fields instead of typing them; paper prescriptions are still typed. Coded dosage instructions on the electronic prescription map to standard label texts, and the aide edits only uncoded instructions. Printing, attaching and the label check stay with the aide, and the pharmacist checks before handing out.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper and faxed prescriptions had to be typed in full.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic prescriptions with coded dosage instructions.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a dose that does not fit the patient.

reach.learn: Whether coded instructions reduce queries from the pharmacy.

evidence.claim: Lab orders and labels can come straight from an order system instead of being retyped.
Medical records are kept 20 years from the last change and shared only with consent.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing labels; dispensing and the pharmacist's check are outside.
Input contract for s1: electronic prescriptions sent by prescribers' systems, about 70% of prescriptions; the rest arrive on paper or by fax and are typed; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s2: dosage instructions coded by the prescriber on the electronic prescription.
Printing and checking keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of prescriptions with coded dosage instructions.
research_questions: Do label errors caught by the pharmacist fall?

already_counted.description: Pharmacy aide checks fields filled from electronic prescriptions.

incremental.description: Pharmacy aide reports wrong code-to-text mappings to the system supplier.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many paper prescriptions from hospitals and dentists; high: mostly electronic prescriptions from GPs with coded instructions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Operate the cash register to process cash or credit sales: call up copayments and scan items, take payment, give receipt and change, and count and reconcile the till.

steps.what: Pharmacy aide scans items and calls up the patient's copayment on the register
Pharmacy aide processes cash or credit payment
Pharmacy aide gives receipt and change
Pharmacy aide counts the register at day end and reconciles cash and card totals

tasks.design: Scanning the prescription bag's barcode pulls the copayment from the pharmacy system into the register, so the aide no longer looks it up and types it. The card terminal is coupled to the register, so the amount is not typed twice. At day end the register shows expected cash and the terminal's card total, and the aide enters the counted cash to see the difference.
tasks.previous_blocker: Copayments were looked up in the pharmacy system and typed into the register and terminal.
tasks.enabler_now: Registers linked to pharmacy systems and coupled card terminals.
tasks.still_hard: Patients disputing a copayment at the counter.
tasks.human_edge: Handling a patient who cannot pay for needed medicine.
tasks.altitude: Less typing; the counter conversation stays.

evidence.claim: Registers can pull amounts from other systems by barcode and pass them to coupled card terminals.
Health data are a special category; care use rests on Art. 9(2)(h).

assumptions: Boundary: counter sales and the day-end till count; banking takings is outside.
Input contract for s1: copayments computed in the pharmacy system during claims processing and a barcode printed on each prescription bag at dispensing.
Input contract for s4: sales totals from the register and card totals from the coupled terminal.
Receipts and change keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of cash against card payments.

incremental.description: Pharmacy aide checks bag barcodes that fail to scan.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly over-the-counter sales and cash; high: mostly prescription pickups paid by card.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
